attributes.body:
Tempus to acquire Personalis for $1.5B.

Shares of both companies plunged following the announcement, which comes less than a year after Tempus acquired digital-pathology company Paige for $81.25 million.

By Eve Bender | July 20, 2026 | 3:03 PM

AI data company Tempus AI announced it will acquire cancer genomics company Personalis in a transaction valued at approximately $1.5 billion.

The acquisition will integrate Personalis' molecular residual disease testing into Tempus' AI precision oncology platform.

Under the definitive agreement, Personalis shareholders will receive $16.25 per share, primarily in Tempus stock. Tempus has the option to pay up to 50% of the consideration in cash.

The purchase price represents a roughly 6% premium over Personalis' closing price Friday and a 28% premium over its unaffected 30-day volume-weighted average share price, according to the companies.

Tempus already owns approximately 12.5% of Personalis.

Shares of both companies fell sharply after the announcement. Tempus AI stock was down nearly 9%, while Personalis shares declined about 12% during Monday morning trading.

The transaction is expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027, subject to approval by Personalis shareholders, regulatory clearances and other customary closing conditions.

The boards of both companies unanimously approved the deal.

Personalis' NeXT Personal platform uses whole-genome sequencing to create a personalized genetic signature of a patient's tumor.

Blood tests can then identify circulating tumor DNA that may remain after treatment or return in the future.

Molecular residual disease (MRD) testing is intended to detect traces of cancer that may be too small to appear on imaging.

"MRD is a large and rapidly growing market with the potential to truly transform how cancer patients are monitored, helping clinicians make faster and more informed decisions when cancer recurs," Eric Lefkofsky, CEO of Tempus, said in a statement.

Tempus said integrating the technology into its platform could help the company support patients from diagnosis and treatment selection through recurrence monitoring.

The acquisition builds on a relationship the companies established in 2023.

Under their agreement, Tempus began offering Personalis' tumor-informed MRD testing to pharmaceutical and biotechnology customers.

The companies expanded the partnership in 2025, allowing Tempus to market NeXT Personal Dx for colorectal cancer.

"We believe this transaction represents an exciting next chapter for Personalis," Chris Hall, CEO of Personalis, said in a statement.

"Combining with Tempus gives us the scale, complementary capabilities and resources to accelerate innovation and deliver even greater value to patients, clinicians and biopharma partners."

THE LARGER TREND

In August 2025, Tempus acquired Paige, an AI-enabled diagnostic platform for oncologists and pathologists, for $81.25 million.

The acquisition expanded Tempus' presence in digital pathology and added Paige's collection of digitized pathology slides, clinical reports and genomic data to its platform.

Earlier that year, the company launched an AI-enabled personal health concierge app that allows patients to aggregate medical records and data from connected health devices.

Tempus has also formed oncology-focused collaborations with pharmaceutical companies. The company partnered with Pfizer to apply AI and machine learning to cancer drug discovery, clinical-trial matching and companion diagnostics.
